newsitem.title: CANADA: Major US carriers slow to match American charge.
newsitem.headline: Major US carriers slow to match American charge.

text.p: Major US airlines were not rushing today to match the fuel surcharge on international cargo shipments planned by American Airlines.
Officials of Northwest Airlines and Continental Airlines said they had no immediate plans to match the surcharge.

"We are currently evaluating our plans and their impact on our customers and will continue to monitor fuel expenses although at this time we do not plan to implement the fuel surcharge," said Diana Bates, director of cargo marketing for Continental Cargo.
Officials of Delta Airlines and United Airlines were not immediately available for comment.

American said it will implement the $0.10/kg surcharge on most of its international network on Nov 15. The surcharge does not cover Pacific routes. A surcharge of C$0.05/kg will be applied from Canada to US points on Nov 25.
